messages:
Anya: Quick sync — I'm putting together a lightweight PRD for the Dedicated Capacity roadmap slice: priority matrix + launch gates for reserved pools, quotas, burst & autoscale. Need alignment by Wednesday.

Anya: TL;DR proposals: 1) per-tenant soft cap with progressive throttling tiers; 2) two-layer burst credits (instant short-burst + queued backfill window); 3) canary rollout gating for quota enforcement; 4) explicit rollback/escape hatch criteria.

Marco: sgtm. Can you drop the doc link?

Anya: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DED-PRD-827 (draft) — main sections: priority matrix, enforcement modes, observability hooks, and launch/pass/fail metrics.

Liz: Heads-up: billing needs the burst credit life cycle defined (when consumed vs when billed) or finance will flag customers. Also we need audit logs per-credit use.

Samir: For autoscale, we should include a pre-warm predictor signal: model of 10m lookahead from request rate + recent cache hit trends. If the predictor triggers, we pre-allocate burst tokens rather than draining pools.

Jia: Suggestion: credits should decay on a sliding window rather than expire abruptly. E.g., decay 20% per 24h so customers don't lose everything after a short spike. Helps customer experience.

Kai: From runtime POV, progressive throttling means changes to request routing and admission. We need a new admission policy flag (soft-throttle -> hard-throttle) and an RPC to signal tenant throttling state to load-balancers. That affects ~3 subsystems.

Anya: Good — I'll add an implementation impact section and required infra changes (routing, telemetry, billing hooks).

Liz: Launch gates proposal: Canary (10% customers for 48h), pass if: p99 latency delta < 5ms, error rate delta < 0.5%, burst credit spend variance < 15%, and no oncall page for quota enforcement.

Samir: Add quality metric: classifier/regression of model output drift for customers who rely on cached context — ensure caching + burst behavior doesn't regress outputs.

Kai: One more runtime constraint: KV-cache eviction interplay during throttles. If we tighten admission too fast, cache churn spikes and latency goes up. Need a smoothing window when moving throttle states.

Jia: Ops ask: make a debug endpoint that returns tenant credit balance + decay schedule + last-consumed-timestamp. That will help support and sales when customers ask.

Anya: Nice. I'll add a minimal JSON debug response shape.

SRE-Bot: reminder: Oncall impact assessment required for any enforcement feature. Add simulated traffic runbook and run a 4h chaos test in staging.

Marco: Action items: Anya to update PRD with: cost/billing lifecycle, audit log schema, debug endpoint sample, runtime flags, and canary metrics. Kai to draft required runtime API changes. Samir + Jia to propose predictor/decay parameters and a simple simulation. Liz to map billing flows and invoice examples.

Anya: I'll schedule a 30m sync Tue 10am PT to finalize gates. If anyone can't make it, drop bullet feedback in the doc by EOD Monday.

Liz: I'll prep two invoice scenarios (startup + enterprise) before the sync.

Kai: I'll push a proto API sketch to the runtime repo and tag you, Anya.

Samir: Will run a small sim comparing immediate credit consumption vs queued backfill and share numbers.

Jia: I'll write the decay math and a customer-facing FAQ blurb.

Anya: Thanks all — linking the draft one more time: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DED-PRD-827. Please add comments inline. :thumbsup:
